# A qualified generic type. `Type` allowed `pkg.Name` or `Name[Args]` and never
# both, so a generic reached through a namespace could not be written at all —
# and resolveQualifiedType discarded the type arguments it was handed, because
# nothing could supply any.
#
# Both halves are fixed: the production admits `pkg.Name[Args]`, the builder
# reads the arguments after the dot-ident rather than returning, and the
# qualified path applies them the way the unqualified one does.
#
# The argument has to reach the field, not just parse. Interpolating `h.item`
# is what asserts that: an unsubstituted `T` reports "type has no string()
# method", so this checking clean is the substitution working.
sngl check main.sngl
stdout 'main.sngl: ok'

# A qualified type that is not generic takes no arguments. The Type production
# only started admitting `pkg.Name[Args]` here, and resolveQualifiedType
# discarded whatever it was handed.
! sngl check arity/main.sngl
stderr 'takes no type arguments'

# A qualified generic in *expression* position: a struct literal may follow
# the bracket after a name, so `b.Holder[int]{…}` is a literal of the
# instance, as a bare `Holder[int]{…}` is.
sngl check lit/main.sngl
stdout 'lit/main.sngl: ok'

-- box/box.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Holder[T any] {
    item T
}

ui.window {
}
-- main.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import b "box"

component show(h b.Holder[int]) node {
    text(value="holding {h.item}")
}

component main node {
    text(value="x")
}

window {
    main
}
-- lit/box/box.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Holder[T any] {
    item T
}

ui.window {
}
-- lit/main.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import b "box"

component main node {
    var h b.Holder[int] = b.Holder[int]{item = 3}
    text(value="{h.item}")
}

window {
    main
}
-- arity/box/box.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Plain {
    n int
}

ui.window {
}
-- arity/main.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import b "box"

component show(p b.Plain[int]) node {
    text(value="{p.n}")
}

window {
}
